tells.1: The oddly chosen 'third plate of the night' feels like manufactured kitchen authenticity; consistency would be more telling late in service.
tells.2: The leap from dinner-only service to 'real days off and nights that actually end' sounds like generic recruitment reassurance unsupported by the stated schedule.
tells.3: Repeated three-part lists and stock recruitment headings make the voice feel templated, especially alongside vague promises like 'a real say.'

reason: Version 1 gives applicants concrete reasons to trust and assess the offer: staffing, covers, a four-day week, covered insurance, and staff histories. Version 2 reads more conversationally than 3, though none of these stylistic signals establishes AI authorship.
